name: Rushikesh L. Kamalapurkar
title: Associate Professor; Director, Systems, Cognition, and Control Laboratory
fitReason: Substantive Bayesian online learning directs real mobile-robot exploration; broader work includes reinforcement learning and data-driven control.

physicalEvidence.summary: April 2026 GP-HT preprint Section VII-C explicitly reports four physical experiments at UF using a Husarion 2R-Pro with Adafruit TSL2591 lux sensor. Measured intensity updates a Gaussian-process posterior; Hough-derived hazard regions modify sampling locations and RRT* routes that the robot executes. It is light-field sensing in the NCR Lab, not radioactive-site deployment or learned low-level motor control. Two- and three-dimensional synthetic field studies are simulation. Early visits to still-unlearned unsafe regions remain possible; no absolute safety claim. Coauthor Trivikram Satharasi is independently identified by SCC as a current UF master’s researcher in the lab; Qureshi/Ogri also appear on its current roster.

shortVisit.summary: Live SCC homepage advertises several PhD positions and asks applicants to explain their graduate-study goals. It lists MS advisees, but no current external-master’s visitor or summer internship invitation was verified.

scoreReasons.fit: Direct probabilistic learning for adaptive robotic exploration, with formal uncertainty-aware control; weaker foundation-model emphasis.
scoreReasons.physical: Four actual UF robot trials; coauthor Satharasi is independently confirmed as current UF SCC master’s researcher, and the other lead student authors are on SCC’s roster. NCR is the named experiment site, not claimed exclusive ownership.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: PhD hiring and local MS supervision do not establish external short-visitor intake.
scoreReasons.freshness: April 2026 primary hardware manuscript and September 2026 official academic activity.
